g1-implement.title: resolver, receipt, and reported degraded mode: implement
g1-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md and dispatch constellation-implementer. Build scripts/map_orient.py with subcommands `orient` and `verify-orientation`: an ordered entrypoint candidate list where RESOLVED requires CITABLE CONTENT rather than mere file existence; a receipt at .agent-work/<work-id>/map-orientation.json with a stated schema; and an exit-code vocabulary that sits ABOVE the argparse/traceback/no-shell collision range (argparse uses 2, tracebacks 1, the engine can synthesize 127). Add the <repo-root> absolute placeholder to init_work_area.resolve_spine and its guard. REQUIRED: tests/test_map_orient.py carrying the mutation floor - the partial-fill matrix (each required degraded field omitted in turn, each asserting refusal, so an all->any mutation fails all three arms) and the could-not-look-versus-no-map discriminator pair differing in exactly one bit. ALSO REQUIRED: tests/test_mutation_floor.py, which mechanically APPLIES each named mutation to a copy of the module, runs the floor, and asserts it goes RED - falsifiability must be demonstrated by execution, not asserted by the party being graded (critic finding 3). ADMIRAL AMENDMENT 1, LOAD-BEARING: the harness MUST ASSERT THE MUTATION APPLIED **BEFORE** it asserts red. Assert the post-mutation source differs from the original (and that the intended replacement is present); if the substitution did not land, FAIL LOUDLY as a harness error rather than reporting a killed mutant. A mutation that silently fails to match produces a green baseline that is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a killed mutant - commander-299 hit exactly this with a non-matching sed this epic. Without the applied-assertion, the check that verifies falsifiability is ITSELF unfalsifiable. Prove you changed the thing, THEN compare (#337).

g3-implement.title: pre-register, delete, then RUN: implement
g3-implement.imperative: STEP 1 - PRE-REGISTER. Write TRIPWIRES.md naming one falsifiable prediction per deletion, and COMMIT IT BEFORE any deletion. Git history is the timestamp proof: it is tamper-evident and needs no clock (the episode writer is deliberately clock-free). Do NOT file episodes yet - `create` requires all five agent-supplied kinds including observed-behavior, and inventing an observation before observing is exactly what this pathway forbids (critic finding 5). STEP 2 - DELETE, in a separate commit: the 86-word dead-path block in COMMANDER_SPINE tasks.context.imperative; the 86-word block in EXECUTE_PLAN tasks.e0-context.imperative; and retarget the pathless 'the current map' phrasing at context and plan. CRITICAL: the phrase 'no docs/agents/ overlay at all' occurs TWICE in tasks.context.imperative - the FIRST is the load-bearing substitute-and-record rule and MUST SURVIVE; delete only the second, inside the dead-path block. STEP 3 - RUN, concretely: materialize a fresh Commander spine in THIS repo via init_work_area.py under a scratch work-id, drive it through init and context with the engine, and capture the engine's own output. Record each observed outcome in .agent-work/issue-304/TRIPWIRE_OUTCOMES.md against the pre-registered prediction by name, citing the pre-registration commit SHA. STEP 4 - FILE the episodes via scripts/apply_episode_delta.py (the ONLY write path), each with expected-behavior = the pre-registered prediction and observed-behavior = what actually happened. STEP 5 - Add tests/test_prose_deletions.py asserting the deleted strings are ABSENT from the shipped templates AND that the surviving substitute-and-record rule is still PRESENT. STEP 6 - Write the corpus-size / per-role-surface trend snapshot to .agent-work/issue-304/TREND_SNAPSHOT.md, derived from git, with a stated schema. ADMIRAL AMENDMENT 2: the snapshot MUST NAME ITS CONSUMER and its successor. The consumer is THE NEXT SNAPSHOT - a baseline's whole purpose is a comparison that does not exist yet, which is legitimate unlike an unread report. State that explicitly, state WHEN the second snapshot is expected (at epic-298 close), and state the retire-if-unread rule: a baseline with no scheduled successor is decoration wearing a measurement's clothes. Same standard already applied to the REPORT-ONLY ordering audit, whose consumer is commander-299's rig during this epic and NOBODY after it.

why_trail.why: Implementer returned a complete result driven through its own engine plan. I re-verified rather than accepting: 80 passed on the required three-file suite, self-test OK, live orient in this repo returns DEGRADED-NO-MAP at exit 10, and it RESOLVES against f1Brainz's real map - both directions exercised. Exit vocabulary 10/11/12/13 sits clear of argparse 2 and traceback 1, confirmed by direct invocation. Amendment 1 was vindicated in fact: the implementer found assertIn would have passed with nothing substituted because mutation 2's replacement text already occurs elsewhere in the module, so the applied-assertion uses a strict count delta.

Reviewer completed the mutation requirement rather than checking conformance: it devised M4 outside the shipped three, applied it, and reported honestly that it SURVIVED. That is a real gap in the floor - single-element filler lists make any and all identical. It also verified the shipped three are behaviorally earned and confirmed the count-delta claim is stronger than reported (both of mutation 2's substitutions have pre-existing replacement text). Verdict BLOCK on a content-level defect I reproduced myself.

Reviewer APPROVE after rework of B1/B2/B3, superseding its own BLOCK. I re-verified independently rather than on report: nonexistent substitute now exits 10 while a real substitute still exits 0 (positive control checked deliberately - a fix that refused everything would produce the first line too), M4 pinned with multi-element filler cases so any and all diverge, required suite 91 passed, self-test exit 0, FULL suite exit 0.
